provenance.expert_method:
Where I looked: the outer wall on the left side of the classroom wing, from the Plant Room at the top to the stair at the bottom. There is no north arrow on this sheet, so I took the top of the sheet as north, which makes the left side west.
Scale: only used to check sizes (scale bar, 0 to 20 m).
Method: I went along the wall from north to south and looked at every gap in the black wall.
Window: a gap with thin parallel lines inside it (the glazing). All of them are the same size, ≈1.30 m wide.
Door: a gap with no lines inside and a swing arc outside, ≈0.92 m wide. There are 4, the classrooms' doors to the outside.
The Plant Room opening at the top has zigzag leaves: a louvred double door, not a window. The doors split the windows into groups: 2, 2, 5, 2, 7 = 18.
Decisions: neighbouring windows are separated by solid wall piers (≈0.5 m), so each one counts as a separate window. Glazed doors would count as doors, but there are none here.
Result: 18. Exact count, if west = left side of the sheet.

Rules a machine can reuse:

Direction words ("west facade"): find the north arrow; if there is none, take the top of the sheet as north and say so.
Window symbol on CAD plans: a gap in the wall with thin parallel lines inside (glazing).
Door symbol: a gap with no lines inside, plus a swing arc.
Wall piers between gaps mean separate windows, even when the windows are the same size and close together.
Sanity check: a facade with classrooms behind it always has windows; 0 is not a plausible answer.
provenance.independent_check: Vector glazing centerlines at x=142.421 pt yield 18 distinct opening spans, matching expert groups 2/2/5/2/7; narrow west-facade crop visually inspected.

title: Entrance sliding doors
question: How many sliding door sets are shown at the Entrance Lobby?
conventions: Count each sliding door set as one opening, regardless of the number of leaves.

provenance.original_question: How many sliding doors are on the whole plan?
provenance.original_how: expert (Ziying, from her written method for dfe-07 at 21:11; marks not exported): the 2 sliding doors of the Entrance Lobby (two opposite arrows)
provenance.evidence_author: AfterQuery curation agent, not human expert
provenance.evidence_method: New boxes from normalized vector geometry/text and visual drawing review; region boxes identify scope, not exhaustive geometric proof.
provenance.expert_method:
Door symbols on this sheet:

One quarter-circle arc with a leaf line = single door.
Two arcs meeting in the middle = double door; it counts as one door opening (two leaves).
A short angled line with no arc = a cupboard or small store door drawn half-open. Whether it is a cupboard or a store depends on the space behind it: a labelled room (e.g. "Store") is a room door, an unlabelled shallow recess off the corridor is a cupboard.
Small zigzag in an outer wall = folding or louvred door. The long zigzag across the Multi-Purpose Hall is a movable partition, not a door.
Two opposite arrows (←→) = sliding door.
Where I looked: the whole plan: the classroom wing, the enclosed walkway and the east wing.
Scale: not needed for counting.
3. Method: split the plan into 9 zones and counted zone by zone so no door was counted twice, using the door symbols in Part A. All doors: classroom wing 65, walkway 3, east wing 60 = 128. Then removed the 13 cupboard doors (short angled leaf, no room label, shallow recess off a corridor). 128 − 13 = 115.
4. Decisions: a door counts only if a person can walk through it. So: cupboard doors are out; WC and shower cubicle doors (11) are in; walk-in Stores drawn with an angled leaf are in, because they are labelled rooms; louvred doors to plant rooms (4) and the sliding doors of the Entrance Lobby (2) are in. The lift is out: a person can enter it, but no door is drawn. The folding partition in the hall is a movable wall, not a door; the small door at its end is in.
5. Result: 115 (±3). Without cubicle doors: 104.
provenance.independent_check: Entrance Lobby crop visually shows two opposing-arrow sliding-door symbols, one inner and one outer opening.
